column3: The Hebrew refers to “him” without naming Gideon; BSB supplies his name.
The Hebrew uses “he said” without repeating Gideon’s name; BSB names him.
The Hebrew calls the princes by name without adding “two” and speaks of their spirit relaxing toward him; BSB calls this their anger subsiding.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names bread loaves and describes the people as “at my feet”; BSB says “my troops” and adds “still” to the pursuing.
The Hebrew uses singular “palm” and singular “your hand”; BSB has plural “hands” and “your possession”.
The Hebrew uses the image “thresh your flesh”; BSB says “tear your flesh”.
The Hebrew says he spoke to them in this way; BSB makes this an explicit request.
The Hebrew says “in peace”; BSB says “in triumph” and explicitly supplies Gideon’s name.
The Hebrew first has plural “their camps” and then singular “the camp of the sons of the east”; BSB reverses these numbers as “army” and “armies”.
The Hebrew describes the route of tent dwellers and says the camp was secure; BSB calls it a caravan route and describes taking the army by surprise.
The Hebrew repeats Zebah and Zalmunna as the captured kings; BSB does not repeat their names there.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “he wrote” without repeating “the young man”; BSB supplies that subject and the noun “names”.
The Hebrew uses singular “palm” and singular “your hand”; BSB has plural “hands” and “your possession”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has plural “sons of the king”; BSB has singular “the son of a king”.
The Hebrew says “he said” without naming Gideon; BSB explicitly names him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “fall upon us”; BSB makes the killing explicit.
The Hebrew repeats “son” in “the son of your son”; BSB uses “grandson”.
The Hebrew repeats “rule over you” in all three clauses; BSB leaves it implicit for Gideon’s son.
The Hebrew explicitly names Gideon and uses pronouns rather than the noun “the enemies”; BSB supplies that noun.
The Hebrew emphasizes giving by repeating its root; BSB renders the emphasis as “gladly”.
The Hebrew does not explicitly name the weight unit “shekels”.
The Hebrew says “it” rather than “all this” and has no explicit “soon” or separate phrase “by worshiping”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he went and lived in his house; BSB specifies returning home.
The Hebrew describes the sons as coming out of his thigh; BSB says “sons of his own”.
